arxiv-2101-08874.title: 5G New Radio for Automotive, Rail, and Air Transport
arxiv-2101-08874.creator: Gábor Fodor ⋆‡ , Julia Vinogradova † , Peter Hammarberg ⋆ , Keerthi Kumar Nagalapur ⋆ , Zhiqiang (Tyler) Qi ♭ , Hieu Do ⋆ , Ricardo Blasco † , Mirza Uzair Baig ⋆ ⋆ Ericsson Research, Sweden, E-mail: firstname.secondname@ericsson.com ‡ KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Sweden. E-mail: gaborf@kth.se
arxiv-2101-08874.description: Abstract The recent and upcoming releases of the 3rd Generation Partnership Project’s 5G New Radio (NR) specifications include features that are motivated by providing connectivity services to a broad set of verticals, including the automotive, rail, and air transport industries.

arxiv-2301-10600.title: Efficiency in local differential privacy
arxiv-2301-10600.creator: Lukas Steinberger
arxiv-2301-10600.description: Abstract We develop a theory of asymptotic efficiency in regular parametric models when data confidentiality is ensured by local differential privacy (LDP). Even though efficient parameter estimation is a classical and well-studied problem in mathematical statistics, it leads to several non-trivial obstacles that need to be tackled when dealing with the LDP case.

arxiv-2307-06982.title: Revisiting the DARPA Communicator Data using Conversation Analysis
arxiv-2307-06982.creator: Peter Wallis
arxiv-2307-06982.description: Abstract Abstract: The state of the art in human computer conversation leaves something to be desired and, indeed, talking to a computer can be down-right annoying. This paper describes an approach to identifying “opportunities for improvement” in these systems by looking for abuse in the form of swear words.

arxiv-2401-01375.title: Mapping Walnut Water Stress with High Resolution Multispectral UAV Imagery and Machine Learning
arxiv-2401-01375.creator: Kaitlyn Wang, Yufang Jin *
arxiv-2401-01375.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Kaitlyn Wang, Yufang Jin *. Effective monitoring of walnut water status and stress level across the whole orchard is an essential step towards precision irrigation management of walnuts, a significant crop in California. This study presents a machine learning approach using Random Forest (RF) models to map stem water potential (SWP) by integrating high-resolution multispectral remote sensing imagery from Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) flights with weather data.

arxiv-2502-04239.title: The Equation of State of QCD up to very high temperatures
arxiv-2502-04239.creator: Leonardo Giusti
arxiv-2502-04239.description: Abstract We present the non-perturbative computation of the entropy density in QCD for temperatures ranging from 3 GeV up to the electro-weak scale, using N f = 3 N_{f}=3 flavours of massless O ( a ) (a) -improved Wilson fermions.

arxiv-2510-06885.title: Measurement of the 35 Cl ( n , p ) (n,p) 35 S cross-section at the CERN n_TOF facility from subthermal energy to 120 keV
arxiv-2510-06885.creator: Marco Antonio Martinez-Cañadas, Pablo Torres-Sánchez, Javier Praena, Ignacio Porras, Marta Sabaté-Gilarte, Oliver Aberle, Victor Alcayne, Simone Amaducci, Józef Andrzejewski, Laurent Audouin, Vicente Bécares, Victor Babiano-Suarez, Michael Bacak, Massimo Barbagallo, František Bečvář, Giorgio Bellia,
arxiv-2510-06885.description: Abstract Background: The 35 Cl ( n , p ) (n,p) 35 S reaction is of special interest in three different applications. First, in Boron Neutron Capture Therapy due to the presence of 35 Cl in brain and skin tissue. Second, it is involved in the creation of 36 S, whose astrophysical origin remains unresolved.

arxiv-2510-14745.title: Transport with noise in dilute gases: Effect of Langevin thermostat on transport coefficients.
arxiv-2510-14745.creator: A. Alés, J. I. Cerato, L. Marchioni and M. Hoyuelos
arxiv-2510-14745.description: Abstract In dilute gases, transport properties such as the thermal conductivity, self-diffusion, and viscosity are significantly affected by interatomic collisions, which are determined by the potential form. This study explores these transport properties in the presence of a Langevin thermostat in systems where particles interact through various potentials, including soft-core and hard-core potentials, both with and without an attractive region.

arxiv-2511-17271.title: Detecting Performance-Relevant Changes in Configurable Software Systems
arxiv-2511-17271.creator: Sebastian Böhm, Florian Sattler, Norbert Siegmund, Sven Apel
arxiv-2511-17271.description: Abstract . Performance is a volatile property of a software system and, as the system evolves, its performance behavior may change, too. As a consequence, frequent performance profiling is required to keep the knowledge about a software system’s performance behavior up to date. Repeating all performance measurements after every revision is a cost-intensive task, though.

europmc-pmc10196242.description: A growing body of research suggests that short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), metabolites produced by intestinal symbiotic bacteria that ferment dietary fibers (DFs), play a crucial role in the health status of symbiotes. pmc-11303394.title: Measurement of hepatic glucose (18F-fluorodeoxyglucose) uptake with positron emission tomography-magnetic resonance imaging in fumonisin B intoxicated rabbit bucks
pmc-11303394.creator: András Szabó, Miklós Emri, Zoltán Tóth, Dániel Fajtai, Tamás Donkó, Örs Petneházy, Dénes Kőrösi, Imre Repa, Alíz Takács, Tímea Kisiván, Zsolt Gerencsér, Omeralfaroug Ali, Janka Turbók, Brigitta Bóta, Patrik Gömbös, Róbert Romvári, Melinda Kovács
pmc-11303394.description: Rabbit bucks (bodyweight 5 kg) underwent dietary intoxication with fumonisin B series mycotoxins (FB1 + FB2 + FB3, 15 mg/kg diet) for 14 days to test the applicability of positron emission tomography-magnetic resonance (PET MR) hybrid imaging in characterizing experimentally induced mild hepatotoxicosis.

pmc-11536352.title: Patterns of animal rabies in the Nizhny Novgorod region of Russia (2012–2022): the analysis of risk factors
pmc-11536352.creator: Olga I. Zakharova, Elena A. Liskova
pmc-11536352.description: IntroductionAnimal rabies is a viral disease that poses a significant threat to domestic and wild animal populations, with devastating consequences for animal health and human life. Understanding and assessing the risk factors associated with the transmission and persistence of the rabies virus in wild and domestic animal populations is crucial for developing effective strategies to control and mitigate cases.

pmc-12501959.title: Spatiotemporal Activity Disruption of Wild Ungulates by Co‐Occurring Livestock: A Case Study in Xinjiang Kanas National Nature Reserve, China
pmc-12501959.creator: Yuhang Zhu, Zhixiang Wang, Yunchuan Dai, Wancai Xia, Fan Wang, Hanlan Fei, Xueyu Wang, Dayong Li
pmc-12501959.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The spatiotemporal differentiation within habitats plays a crucial role in shaping community diversity and coexistence mechanisms. Exploring how species with similar ecological niches coexist remains a fundamental problem in ecology. We utilized infrared camera data to study the spatiotemporal activity patterns and interspecies interactions of three wild ungulates and sympatric livestock—red deer ( Cervus elaphus ), roe deer ( Capreolus pygargus ), wild boar ( Sus scrofa ), and cattle ( Bos taurus)—in Xinjiang Kanas National Nature Reserve, China.

pmc-12576650.title: Motor Function in Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy R1/2A
pmc-12576650.creator: Meredith K. James, Megan A. Iammarino, Natalie F. Reash, Christopher L. Steiner, Audrey B. Knight, Melissa A. Smith, Dionne Moat, Jassi Michell-Sodhi, Karen S.W. Wong, Emma Grover, Emma-Jayne Robinson, Anna G. Mayhew, Michelle Eagle, Maha Elseed, Michela Guglieri, Volker Straub, Chiara Marini-Bettol
pmc-12576650.description: Background and ObjectivesLimb-girdle muscular dystrophy (LGMD) type R1/2A, calpain-3–related, is a rare, autosomal recessive disorder caused by pathogenic variants in the CAPN3 gene. LGMDR1/2A causes progressive weakness of upper and lower limbs, leading to difficulty walking and use of arms for overhead activities.

pmc-12622504.title: Cancer: From a Genetic Disorder to a Systemic Disease
pmc-12622504.creator: Ada Hang‐Heng Wong, Yuming Hu
pmc-12622504.description: ore research is needed as new pathways are unraveled during cancer initiation, progression, and metastasis. Future research calls us to dive deeper into the mechanisms of cancer etiology, understand the tumor macroenvironment, decipher the cancer exposomics, adopt a holistic approach to cancer treatment, and explore new clinician‐patient dynamics.

pmc-12653665.title: Comparative Ultrastructure and Ecological Adaptation of Adhesive Setae in Four Species of Longhorn Beetles (Coleoptera)
pmc-12653665.creator: Zheng Liu, Yuan-Yuan Lu, Mei-Ying Lin, Roberto Romani
pmc-12653665.description: Simple SummaryLonghorn beetles are known to infest a variety of plants, such as trees, flowers, and crops. These insects frequently move on vertical trunks and on the undersides of leaves, aided by specialized microscopic setae that are adhesive and located on the ventral sides of their tarsi.

pmc-12731587.title: SS18::SSX and BRD9 Modulate Synovial Sarcoma Differentiation
pmc-12731587.creator: Anna Kuntze, Victor Banerjee, Marcel Trautmann, Charlotte Pünt, Ruth Berthold, Pascal Hauser, Lucas Scholl, Eva Wardelmann, Kornelius Kerl, Wolfgang Hartmann, Ilka Isfort
pmc-12731587.description: Highlights What are the main findings? SS18::SSX and BRD9 mediate E-Cadherin repression through regulation of Snail and Slug.SS18::SSX stabilizes Snail protein by preventing proteasomal degradation.BRD9 controls key pathways governing synovial sarcoma differentiation. What is the implication of the main finding? Multilayered regulation of EMT factors by SS18::SSX and BRD9 contributes to the cellular phenotype in synovial sarcoma.

pmc-13070908.title: Modeling the effects of routine screening for accidental lab-acquired infections on the risk of potential pandemic pathogen escape from high-biosafety research facilities
pmc-13070908.creator: Byron Cohen, Boyu Ren, William Hanage, Nicolas Menzies, Kevin Croke
pmc-13070908.description: IntroductionAccidental lab-acquired infections (LAIs) risk releasing potential pandemic pathogens from high-biosafety (BSL-3 or BSL-4) research facilities. We constructed a stochastic network infectious disease model to simulate how following an initial LAI, the probability of an outbreak of a pathogen resembling wild-type SARS-COV-2 would be influenced by test-and-isolate interventions over a 100-day horizon.

pmc-13183224.title: “We do anything to get alcohol”: A mixed methods approach to explore the intersections between alcohol use and HIV risk and infection amongst adolescent girls and young women from high HIV-burdened communities in South Africa
pmc-13183224.creator: Kate Bergh, Zoe Duby, Jeroen De Man, Nabila Ebrahim, Caroline Kuo, Carl Lombard, Petal Petersen Williams, Kim Jonas
pmc-13183224.description: Despite national declines in HIV prevalence, adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) in South Africa continue to face a disproportionate burden of HIV infection. The syndemic theory provides a framework for understanding how interconnected epidemics such as alcohol use disorders, violence and HIV cluster together and reinforce each other.

pmc-13223609.title: Integrated transcriptomics and metabolomics reveal the effects of chronic alcohol consumption on periodontitis in rats
pmc-13223609.creator: Zirui Zhao, Zixuan Zhao, Yaqian Zhai, Jingyuan Sun, Na Liu, Qing Liu
pmc-13223609.description: IntroductionChronic alcohol consumption exacerbates the progression of periodontitis, the sixth most prevalent global disease affecting over 740 million people, though its underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood.ObjectiveThe study aims to elucidate the impact and mechanisms of chronic alcohol consumption on periodontitis in rats through integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses.

pmc-13293383.title: Shy or bold, all get caught: Two active capture methods show no behavioural bias in a large herbivore
pmc-13293383.creator: Rudy Brogi, Francesca Brivio, Sabrina Manera, Bastien Saladini, Marco Apollonio

pmc-13460079.title: Complete genome sequence of multidrug-resistant Edwardsiella ictaluri A21-00102 isolated from channel catfish (Ictalurus punctatus) in the United States
pmc-13460079.creator: Rideeta Islam Aishy, Fenny Patel, Anna Collinsgru, Mark L. Lawrence, Larry A. Hanson, Stephen R. Reichley, Hasan C. Tekedar
pmc-13460079.description: Edwardsiella ictaluri is the causative agent of enteric septicemia of catfish, a major disease associated with high mortality and economic loss in U.S. aquaculture. Here, we report the complete genome sequence of E. ictaluri A21-00102, a multidrug-resistant strain, consisting of a chromosome of 3,829,734 bp and three plasmids.

pmc-13679776.title: New challenges in horticultural IPM: artificial intelligence can enhance the use of biocontrol agents
pmc-13679776.creator: Andrea Lovazzano, Rashmi Mishra, Dr. Mushtaque Ahmed Rahu, Yufeng Yang
pmc-13679776.description: Modern horticulture faces the dual imperatives of increasing global food production while mitigating the severe environmental and health impacts of conventional chemical pesticides. Biological control agents (BCAs), which utilize beneficial microorganisms, macroorganisms, semiochemical and botanicals to suppress pathogens, represent a cornerstone of sustainable agriculture but have been historically constrained by inconsistent field performance, high specificity, and slow action.
